HYE04MON0U_C970.title: Book: Dior, La Légende du 30 Avenue Montaigne
HYE04MON0U_C970.description: Celebrating the reopening of 30, avenue Montaigne and the opening of La Galerie Dior, this book shows the public and unprecedented history of the hallmark Haute Couture House headquarters. 30 Montaigne has been tied to Dior since its founding in 1946. Christian Dior chose this hôtel particulier as the home to his Couture House and the backdrop of his collection presentations, including the inaugural fashion show in 1947 that marked the debut of the New Look era. Since then, Christian Dior and his successors – from Yves Saint Laurent to Maria Grazia Chiuri – have designed and created all of the House collections there. 30 Montaigne still maintains its ateliers, making it a legendary address of Parisian Haute Couture. Looking at iconic images of Mr. Dior working in his design studio, fittings, backstage at shows, archival documents and a stunning portfolio of Dior creations, readers will experience the spirit of 30 Montaigne through the decades and get a peek into its future. Text by Maureen Footer, Jérôme Hanover and Olivier Flaviano.

HYE04MRP0U_C970.title: Book: Dior Metamorphosis
HYE04MRP0U_C970.description: The reinvention of 30 Montaigne, photographed by Robert Polidori, captures a gripping journey between past, present and future. Following the reopening of 30 Montaigne, Dior Metamorphosis unveils never-before-seen photographs by Robert Polidori, one of the greatest contemporary photographers and a privileged witness to the restoration of Christian Dior Couture's historic home. Throughout two years of renovations, Robert Polidori followed the various phases of deconstruction and resurrection, creating images that invite us behind the scenes to see the guts of this marvelous refuge, as Christian Dior called it. From the raw setting of debris and dust, light and beauty spring from these unique images. Reflecting reinvention, hallmark House designs — like the signature Bar suit — are featured amid the construction, an artistic statement imbued with Mr. Dior's soul and the ethos of the House. The timeless architecture of the silhouettes acts as a powerful omen for building the fashion and the world of tomorrow. Text by Emanuele Coccia. Photographs by Robert Polidori.

HYE04LFD0U_C970.title: Book: Dior Scarves. Fashion Stories
HYE04LFD0U_C970.description: An affectionate atlas of Dior scarves at the heart of iconic fashion. A scarf unfurls over the back of the book's dust jacket. The paper inside is as light and soft as silk. From Christian Dior to Maria Grazia Chiuri, the scarves convey the imagination of the creative directors who have shaped the haute couture house. Featuring over 400 designs, primarily taken from the Dior archives, the book traces a remarkable history of fashion. Sophisticated, minimalist, figurative, abstract, luxurious, essential, contemporary and timeless designs for men and women. Dior silk scarves form an incomparable visual repertoire, sure to appeal to any connoisseur of fashion, design and the decorative arts. In addition to this compendium of scarves, enriched with photography portfolios by Brigitte Niedermair and Pol Baril, the book includes content from leading art and fashion historians — Maria Luisa Frisa, Claire Allen-Johnstone, Émilie Hammen, Elda Danese. The foreword is by Maria Grazia Chiuri, Creative Director of Dior Women's collections.

HYE04DJG0U_C970.title: Book: Dior by John Galliano
HYE04DJG0U_C970.description: DIOR BY JOHN GALLIANO (1997-2011) is the fifth volume in the DIOR BY collection, which explores the lines of each Creative Director at Christian Dior Couture. Before joining Dior as Creative Director of the Women's collection, Gibraltar-born British designer John Galliano had already encountered an array of artists and dynamic characters with whom he forged strong bonds. These kindred spirits would go on to play a defining role in his career. From the moment he joined Dior, Galliano set himself apart with his flamboyant shows, blending eclectic historical and cultural inspirations — a global kaleidoscope of influences and an unbridled form of creativity, steeped in romance and heritage. The designer's sensitivity to haute couture savoir-faire and his innate sense of the spectacular earned him a reputation as a master of the silhouette. Galliano reinvented the art — and the essence — of haute couture, redefining the codes of contemporary style by drawing on influences of his travels — both real and imagined — with the impressive legacy of Christian Dior. This book showcases the exceptional silhouettes he created for Dior, featuring his most iconic designs, photographed by Laziz Hamani, together with shots by Steven Meisel, Annie Leibovitz, Irving Penn and Paolo Roversi.

In 2012, Raf Simons is chosen to usher in a new era of the House's history. He breathes contemporary inspiration into Dior's romantic heritage by marrying his signature minimal aesthetic with the House's poetic elegance. A graduate in industrial design and furniture design from Belgium, Raf Simons brings his unique sensibility to fashion, infusing it with the eclectic mix of music, performance and fine arts that is inherent in his creative process. Of all the major Parisian Houses, Dior holds the most prestige around the world. Dior by Raf Simons — the sixth installment of the collection dedicated to Dior's creative directors — celebrates the most remarkable creations from Fall-Winter 2012 to Fall-Winter 2015, magnificently photographed by Laziz Hamani and explored by fashion journalist Tim Blanks. HYE04RMG0U_C400.description: This gorgeous book is a compilation of works by the illustrator Mats Gustafson of Maria Grazia Chiuri's collections for Dior. Seven years after the publication of the Dior volume by Mats Gustafson, the Swedish illustrator revisits the sophistication and glamour of the Maison Dior. In this volume, his ethereal watercolors and vibrantly colored collages exclusively depict creations by Maria Grazia Chiuri, Dior's Creative Director since 2016. The book assembles Chiuri's most emblematic styles, from her first to her latest Haute Couture and Ready-to-Wear collections. Drawings of motif details and accessories — such as bags, shoes, and perfume bottles, among others — enhance the selection of looks. Celebrating the House's creativity, Mats Gustafson's illustrations capture Maria Grazia Chiuri's innovations while showcasing the timeless charm of Dior. Reviving the tradition of fashion illustration with an inventive flair, Mats Gustafson delivers an invaluable graphic body of work that will satisfy any fan of fashion and art. HYE04DCR0U_C000.title: Book: Christian Dior – Designer of Dreams
HYE04DCR0U_C000.description: Christian Dior presented his first fashion show in 1947, marking the end of wartime austerity and the birth of a new feminine silhouette. Featuring a cinched waist, full skirt and soft shoulders, this silhouette was inspired by the so-called 'femmes fleurs' who embodied quintessential Parisian luxury. The 'New Look' repositioned Paris as the fashion capital and made the Dior name synonymous with haute couture. This book details a selection of 70 silhouettes created by Christian Dior and his successors — Yves Saint Laurent, Marc Bohan, Gianfranco Ferré, John Galliano, Raf Simons and Maria Grazia Chiuri. Specially photographed for this book, these garments are accompanied by texts contextualizing them, sketches, photographs of fashion shows and the work of the greatest fashion photographers, including Irving Penn, Richard Avedon, Cecil Beaton, Helmut Newton, Patrick Demarchelier, Peter Lindbergh, Mario Testino and Nick Knight. The texts highlight the defining themes of the House's history: lines, architecture, links to history and art, color, gardens and other inspiration, as well as the brand's muses and celebrated clients (Marlene Dietrich, Grace of Monaco, Marilyn Monroe, Elizabeth Taylor, Lady Diana, Charlize Theron, Natalie Portman, Jennifer Lawrence, etc.).

HYE04BRI0U_C970.title: Book: Photography, Christian Dior by Brigitte Niedermair
HYE04BRI0U_C970.description: The book Photography, Christian Dior by Brigitte Niedermair explores photographer Brigitte Niedermair's unique collaboration with the House. The remarkable relationship between Maria Grazia Chiuri, creative director of Christian Dior Couture womenswear, and Brigitte Niedermair is expressed through ingeniously provocative and unconventional photographs. Brigitte Niedermair has delved deep into the extensive Dior archives and selected around 40 historical pieces, each of which has been photographed twice with a silver-box camera in a five-by-four-inch format. Hidden details are revealed about the construction of designs including jackets, coats, day outfits, and evening dresses to offer a unique perspective. The book features a preface by Maria Grazia Chiuri and is enriched with contributions from Olivier Gabet, Brigitte Lacombe, and Maripol, as well as artists and designers Martino Gamper and Marcello Jori.

HYE04DJO0U_C970.title: Book: Dior Joaillerie (The A to Z of Victoire de Castellane)
HYE04DJO0U_C970.description: Dior Joaillerie offers readers an immersion into the heart of the work of the creative director, Victoire de Castellane. Drawing its inspiration from a blend of pop culture, plant motifs and couture details, her work reflects a playful world in which diamond bows are reminiscent of untied ribbons, ladybugs are lacquered and rings blossom like flowers. Multicolored opals and sapphires reinvent sea creatures while snakes, salamanders and frogs are made of rubies, sapphires and emeralds. Skulls wear crowns of diamonds and roses are adorned in beautiful ballgowns. This first work devoted to the talent of the Place Vendôme jeweler showcases the savoir-faire and aesthetics of the Dior jewelry collections. The scholarly and poetic text by jewelry historian Michèle Heuzé plunges into the world of French luxury and refinement.

HYE04CDD1U_C970.title: Book: Christian Dior Designer of Dreams, クリスチャン・ディオール、夢のクチュリエ, Exhibition in Japan
HYE04CDD1U_C970.description: This seminal book retraces the inter-linkages between the House of Dior and Japan in an unprecedented way. Published on the occasion of the exhibition Christian Dior: Designer of Dreams opening December 21, 2022, at the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT), this title chronicles the evolution of the House of Dior from its first collection in 1947 in Paris, when Christian Dior heralded the birth of a new era of elegance with his revolutionary 'New Look,' to the present day. Furthermore, this book underlines the links between the House of Dior and Japan, with a magnificent portfolio of original photographs by the famous Japanese photographer Yuriko Takagi. The book includes new and original texts: a foreword by Motoyuki Oka, Director of the Museum of Contemporary Art in Tokyo, and Pietro Beccari, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Christian Dior Couture; an introduction by Florence Müller, curator of the exhibition; contributions by Kazuko Koike, Creative Director; Akiko Fukai, Honorary Curator, The Kyoto Costume Institute; Kaya Tsujita, Fashion Historian, Doctor of History, École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales; Vincent Leret, Heritage Manager, Parfums Christian Dior; and Olivier Flaviano, Head of La Galerie Dior.
